answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable stake that only matures after proven work, so making thousands of fakes costs real capital and time. A new agent starts on the velvet edge of trust, trading only small amounts until peers attest its deliveries. Reputation then grows like a terrace: each verified job adds a step that raises its limits, while failures cut it back. A shared wharf log records every completed task, so one operator running many sock puppets cannot hide identical behavior, and honest agents can check the ledger before paying.
